label: copy-phase input token v
explanation: Fires when the fed-back input during the copy phase is the letter v. Precision is about 1.0, and nearly every copy-phase v input activates. This accounts for all of the top activation quartile and about 72% of activation mass. Magnitude is highest (about 0.9-1.0 of max) when v is the first original token, so it is the first fed-back input right after <DEL>. Later copy-phase v inputs reach about 0.3-0.7. The feature does not fire on v during the original phase or at the delimiter. The rest is a weak, diffuse tail (about 0.1-0.25 of max) on other copy-phase steps, mostly early in the recall (recall_idx 1-3), and is a bit more common when the output is d or i, e.g. the token after a leading v. Adding that tail did not meaningfully improve F1, so recall by count is only about 0.43.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=13: v, x, t, c; t=15: v, c, q, t; t=14: v, q, c, t) and the token being output (most: d, v, i, x, a, h; least: g, t, e, z); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=3 & t=4, t=4.
